7-8.name: Lectures 7–8
7-8.subtitle: Lewis structures, formal charge, resonance and the octet rule
7-8.ref_html:
Formulas

  • Formal charge = group valence − lone-pair electrons − number of bonds
  • Electron count on A (counting up) = valence e⁻ of A + bonds − formal charge
  • Nonbonding electrons on A (counting down) = valence e⁻ of A − bonds − formal charge
  • Bond order = shared electron pairs between two atoms, averaged over resonance structures
  • Sum of formal charges = overall charge of the species
  • Apparent electron count of hypervalent ABₙ = valence e⁻ of A + number of single bonds

Conventions

  • Double bond counts as 2 bonds, triple bond as 3 bonds
  • Valence electrons = old group number (I–VIII) = last digit of new group number
  • Octet rule: 8 e⁻
  • Duet rule (H): 2 e⁻
  • Transition elements: 18 e⁻

9-10.name: Lectures 9–10
9-10.subtitle: Oxidation numbers, VSEPR, polarity, light and black-body radiation
9-10.ref_html:
Formulas

  • Unknown oxidation number = overall charge − Σ(known oxidation numbers)
  • Steric number SN = CN (bonded atoms) + LP (lone pairs)
  • AXₓEₑ with x + e = SN
  • c = νλ (ν = c/λ, λ = c/ν)
  • E = hν = hc/λ
  • Planck oscillator energies: ε = nhν (n = 0, 1, 2, …)
  • Wien's law: T·λmax = constant
  • Stefan's law: total intensity ∝ T⁴

Constants

  • h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s
  • c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹
  • NA = 6.022 × 10²³ mol⁻¹
  • Wien constant = 2.90 × 10⁻³ m K
  • 1 nm = 10⁻⁹ m
  • 1 μm = 10⁻⁶ m

11.name: Lecture 11
11.subtitle: Photoelectric effect, line spectra and the Bohr model
11.ref_html:
Formulas

  • Photon energy: E = hν = hc/λ
  • Wavelength and frequency: c = λν
  • Photoelectric effect: KE = hν − Φ
  • Work function: Φ = hν₀
  • Threshold wavelength: λ₀ = hc/Φ
  • Balmer formula: ν = C(1/2² − 1/n²), n = 3, 4, 5, 6
  • Rydberg: 1/λ = RH (1/n₁² − 1/n₂²), n₂ > n₁
  • Bohr angular momentum: mₑvr = nh/2π = nħ
  • Bohr radius: rₙ = n²a₀/Z
  • Bohr energy: Eₙ = −RE Z²/n²
  • Transition energy: ΔE = RE (1/n₁² − 1/n₂²) = hν = hc/λ
  • Resonance condition: E(photon) = hν = E₂ − E₁
  • RE = hcRH

Constants

  • h = 6.626 × 10⁻³⁴ J·s
  • c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m/s
  • RH = 1.097 × 10⁷ m⁻¹ (lecture rounds to 1.10 × 10⁷ m⁻¹)
  • RE = 2.18 × 10⁻¹⁸ J = 13.6 eV
  • a₀ = 0.529 Å

Hydrogen series

  • Lyman: n₁ = 1, ultraviolet
  • Balmer: n₁ = 2, visible (656, 486, 434, 410 nm)
  • Paschen: n₁ = 3, infrared

ch12.name: Chapter 12
ch12.subtitle: Electromagnetic radiation, the nature of matter, the hydrogen spectrum and the Bohr model
ch12.ref_html:
Formulas

  • Wavelength and frequency: λν = c
  • Planck quantization: ΔE = nhν (n = 1, 2, 3, …)
  • Photon energy: E = hν = hc/λ
  • Threshold energy: E₀ = hν₀
  • Photoelectron kinetic energy: KE = ½mv² = hν − hν₀
  • Einstein: E = mc², so m = E/c²
  • de Broglie wavelength: λ = h/mv
  • Bohr energy levels: E = −2.178 × 10⁻¹⁸ J (Z²/n²)
  • Transition energy: ΔE = E_final − E_initial = −2.178 × 10⁻¹⁸ J (1/n_final² − 1/n_initial²)
  • Emitted or absorbed wavelength: λ = hc/|ΔE|

Constants

  • h = 6.626 × 10⁻³⁴ J·s
  • c = 2.9979 × 10⁸ m/s
  • 1 Hz = 1 s⁻¹
  • 1 J = 1 kg·m²/s²
  • NA = 6.022 × 10²³ mol⁻¹
  • Ionization energy of ground-state H = 2.178 × 10⁻¹⁸ J per atom

ch13.name: Chapter 13
ch13.subtitle: Bond energies, Lewis structures, resonance, octet exceptions, formal charge and VSEPR
ch13.ref_html:
Formulas

  • ΔH = ΣD(bonds broken) − ΣD(bonds formed)
  • Formal charge = valence e⁻ on free atom − valence e⁻ assigned in the molecule
  • Valence e⁻ assigned = lone-pair electrons + ½(shared electrons)
  • Sum of formal charges = overall charge of the molecule or ion

Rules

  • Bond breaking is endothermic (+); bond forming is exothermic (−)
  • Bond energies give approximate ΔH, for gas-phase reactions only
  • Lewis step 1: sum all valence electrons
  • Lewis step 2: one electron pair per bond between bound atoms
  • Lewis step 3: place remaining electrons to satisfy the duet rule (H) and octet rule (second row)
  • B and Be are often electron-deficient; second-row elements never exceed an octet
  • Third-row and heavier elements may exceed an octet
  • Extra electrons go on the central atom
  • Best structure (second row): formal charges near zero, negative charge on the most electronegative atom
  • Lone pairs need more room than bonding pairs and compress bond angles
  • Multiple bonds count as one effective electron pair in VSEPR

VSEPR geometries

  • 2 pairs: linear, 180°
  • 3 pairs: trigonal planar, 120°
  • 4 pairs: tetrahedral, 109.5° (AB₃ trigonal pyramidal, AB₂ V-shaped)
  • 5 pairs: trigonal bipyramidal, 90° and 120° (AB₄ see-saw, AB₃ T-shaped, AB₂ linear)
  • 6 pairs: octahedral, 90° (AB₄ with 2 lone pairs: square planar)
  • Bond angles: CH₄ 109.5°, NH₃ 107°, H₂O 104.5°

psych-3-5.name: Chapters 3–5
psych-3-5.subtitle: Consciousness · Nature, nurture and human diversity · Development
psych-3-5.ref_html:
Three running frames

  • Ch 3: consciousness as a narrator: reads the script aloud, takes credit, only sometimes edits
  • Ch 4: universal grammar (shared, evolved) vs local dialect (genes, experience, culture)
  • Ch 5: what the child brings vs what experience adds

Four properties of consciousness (Ch 3)

  • Intentionality: directed toward an object (always about something)
  • Unity: senses integrated into one coherent whole
  • Selectivity: includes some things, leaves others out (cocktail-party phenomenon)
  • Transience: constantly changing

Sleep stages and EEG (Ch 3)

  • Awake: beta waves (alpha when relaxed and drowsy)
  • Stage 1: theta waves; hypnagogic state
  • Stage 2: sleep spindles and K-complexes
  • Stages 3–4: delta waves; deep slow-wave sleep; severe sleep inertia if woken
  • REM: fast sawtooth waves like waking; vivid dreams; muscle atonia
  • Across the night: deep sleep early, REM periods longer later

Drug classes and neurotransmitters (Ch 3)

  • Alcohol (depressant): increases GABA
  • Stimulants: raise dopamine and norepinephrine
  • Opiates (narcotics): mimic endorphins
  • THC (marijuana): acts on anandamide receptors

Attachment styles (Ch 5)

  • Secure (51.6%): explores, upset at departure, calms quickly at reunion; sensitive, responsive caregiving
  • Avoidant (14.7%): ignores or turns away at reunion, hidden stress; caregiver rebuffs bids for comfort
  • Ambivalent / resistant (10.2%): clings yet pushes away, hard to soothe; inconsistent caregiving
  • Disorganized (23.5%): no consistent strategy; frightening or frightened caregiver

Piaget's stages (Ch 5)

  • Sensorimotor (birth–2): senses and actions; object permanence, stranger anxiety
  • Preoperational (2–6/7): words and images, no logical operations; egocentrism, no conservation
  • Concrete operational (7–11): logic about concrete events; conservation, reversibility
  • Formal operational (12+): abstract, hypothetical reasoning

Kohlberg's levels (Ch 5)

  • Preconventional (before ~9): self-interest, avoid punishment or gain reward
  • Conventional (early adolescence): approval, social order, laws
  • Postconventional (only some people): principles above laws; requires formal operations
  • Scored on the reasoning, not the steal / don't-steal answer

8-9.name: Lectures 8–9
8-9.subtitle: Drawing rules, resonance, octet exceptions, oxidation numbers, VSEPR and polarity
8-9.ref_html:
Formulas

  • Formal charge = valence e⁻ − lone-pair electrons − number of bonds
  • Electron count on A = valence e⁻ of A + number of bonds − formal charge
  • Nonbonding electrons on A = valence e⁻ of A − number of bonds − formal charge
  • Unknown oxidation number = charge on species − Σ(known oxidation numbers)
  • Steric number SN = CN (atoms bonded) + LP (lone pairs); VSEPR notation AXₓEₑ with x + e = SN

Conventions

  • Common valence (bonds needed to fill the valence shell, from XHₙ): H 1, F 1, Cl 1, O 2, N 3, C 4
  • Double bond counts as 2 bonds, triple bond as 3 bonds (for electron counts); a multiple bond counts as one domain in VSEPR
  • Oxidation numbers: element = 0; F always −1; O usually −2 (not with F or in O–O bonds); H +1 with nonmetals, −1 with metals, B or Si
  • SN 2 linear · 3 trigonal planar · 4 tetrahedral · 5 trigonal bipyramidal · 6 octahedral · 7 pentagonal bipyramidal
